vnode algorithm occasionally generates imbalanced rings
Generally, the deterministic vnode algorithm seems to make OK decisions, but I've been working on a cluster where the tokens it's generated look like they're not much better than random.  I've verified `allocate_tokens_for_local_replication_factor=3` was used when the nodes were bootstrapped via the logs.

I've parsed the nodetool ring output and added some additional info so it's obvious where the ranges are imbalanced.  I've calculated the range for each token along with the avg range for each token range in the cluster, and listed each range size relative to the average as the %.  For example:

The node that owns the token -5646866338711190221, that range is only 9.23% of the average token range in the cluster.

 
{noformat}
37   10.20.80.11      rack-b    -5646866338711190221        9455879439619330 9.23%    347209701613153318 112.93%{noformat}
Looking at the below data, it's obvious that some nodes have way more data (272622351113636532 266.02%) than they should.

It doesn't look like we're trying to balance the ring by picking tokens that split the largest ranges, which explains why the most recent node I we added had less than half of the data as the largest node.
